THANG 1. Simon Says F3 (5 min.) 
Q calls out various exercises, which will all be on Q. Q will vary the cadence to try to catch PAX. If they mess up, they squat or plank till the end. 

THANG 2. Red Light, Green Light (3 rounds)
The winner of Simon Says is designated as the "stoplight." The stoplight stands about 300 feet away at a specific finish line. The stoplight calls out "green light!" which signals the players to begin moving toward them. Then, the stoplight yells, "red light!" and if any PAX is caught moving when the stoplight turns around, that PAX does air squats till the end of the round. The game is over when all the players are out or pass the stoplight. The first PAX to reach the stoplight gets to be the stoplight in the next round.

THANG 3. Everyone’s It Toilet Bowl Tag
PAX were in a 100’ x 100’ coned area and were all “it.” If a PAX got tagged he had to Al Gore till the PAX that tagged him is tagged. 

THANG 4. SPUD
The object of this ball game is to run as far and as fast as possible from the person who is throwing the ball and to dodge the ball when it’s thrown at you without moving your feet.
To start, all PAX formed a tight circle with the Q in the middle, who is the thrower, or "it" first. The thrower tosses the ball straight up into the air. As soon as the ball is released, PAX begin to run away from the thrower. When the thrower catches the ball on its way back down, they yell, "Spud!" at which point players immediately freeze where they are.
The thrower then tries to tag a player with the ball. The frozen player can try to dodge the ball but is not allowed to move their feet. If a player is hit, they will get the letter "S" and move to the middle to be the next thrower. If the thrower does not hit a PAX, he has to run to get the ball while all other PAX run back to the tight circle. (We didn’t spell out any letters but just ran and threw balls at each other).
THANG 5. Merkin Frisbee
PAX took turns throwing the frisbee as far as possible across the field, running to the frisbee and doing 10 merkins, then planking for the six. PAX did this all the way across the field.

We have spent last 12 weeks discussing how to Get Right.  Live Right is the second quadrant of the QSource. It is the HIM’s dedication to Purposefulness.Whereas the first quadrant, the Get Right, was focused on what a man must do to achieve proper personal alignment and Accelerate himself, the Live Right is focused on the HIM’s IMPACT on the lives of other people and how he helps them to Accelerate.

BOHICA

QSource
Because Purpose is outside of oneself, living Purposefully requires self-sacrifice. A man who Commits to Purpose abandons service to himself because he finds that he cannot serve two masters. But a man who has not yet gotten Right, whose boat is still capsized in the river, can only serve himself because he is consumed with his own survival. “Leg-acy” 
Split into pax 1s & 2s. Each Pax group will have a Cindy. Both pax will line up on the side line closest to the track and leave their Cindy on opposite side of the court.
Pax 1: Squat walk (one step, one squat) to opposite sideline. Pax 2 stays put and does a different squat variation every time Pax 1 goes down for a squat. When Pax 1 reaches the other sideline, Pax 1 will do an exercise & 2 will recover. Once Pax 1 comes back then it’s pax 2 and both pax switch roles.
 
First go-around: 
1) 20 Squat thrust with Cindy after doing squat walk.
2) full squats every time their partner goes down for a squat 
Second go-around:
1) 20 Bulgarian squats with Cindy after squat walk
2) on Q squats (when partner goes down for a squat, pax squats down and stays in that position, when partner goes down for another squat, pax goes up).
Third go-around:
1) 40 Goblet squats after completing squat walk.
2) half squat (from half way to all the way down) for every squat their patented does.
Fourth go-around:
1) 50 calve raises after completing squat walk.

QSOURCE 1.12 Meeting
F3's third F is Faith. Faith is the belief in something greater than yourself. A man must be competent in his Faith. Being competent in his faith requires skill. Skill requires practice. Meeting -- like prayer and Study -- is a brick in the practice of Faith.

We all have reasons not to meet, but Meeting has a Purpose. Because of the Flux, all men have have their ups and downs. We spend some of our time on the mountaintop of our Faith-life, when we want to share our Joy with every stranger we meet. But we also have to slog through valleys of spiritual dryness, when all we really want is to be is left alone to lick our wounds.

Ironically, it’s those latter times (when Meeting is the last thing we want to do) that are the instances in which we most need to be there, so that we can share the strength of our Brothers who might just be on their own mountaintop. How much easier it is to reach up from the pit when a Brother is reaching down to meet us.

Thing 2 Cindy Court Pull Throughs- ( Confusing to explain, super easier to see in person) 
PAX will high plank shoulder to shoulder and will cindy pull through the line. We will start on the baseline, with our line extending towards the opposite end of the court. Once the cindy gets to the last guy in front, it will be pulled back through to the first guy at the start. The goal is to cindy pull the length of the entire court, this is accomplished as each time the PAX at the back sprints to the front, the line moves forward until we reach the opposite baseline.

This will be a 45 minute AMRAP, Iron PAX Challenge style beatdown. It is centered completely around getting points.

45 mins is placed onto the clock.
In cadence the Q will warm up in proper form the following exercises: Imperial Walkers, Grass Grabbers, Side Straddle Hops. 4 count cadence, until the count of 10. The proper cadence shall be:
“The next exercise is…” [pause] “Side Straddle Hop!” ( or name of other exercise)
“Starting Position…” [pause] “Move!”
“In Cadence…” [pause] “Exercise!” ( begin count 1..2..3). PAX declares 1.
The beatdown is a 4-spoke workout.
Center is 25 merkins
Sidelines is 25 big boys and 25 yds away from center at the North and South
The 20 yd line, which is 30 yds from the center, is 25 curls.
(YHC had to pace these off due to lack of a football field at The Cave)
One complete counterclockwise cycle through all stations would look as such:
PAX runs 25 yds to the north and does 25 BigBoys
PAX runs 25 yds to the center and does 25 merkins.
PAX runs 30 yds to west and does 25 curls
PAX runs 30 yds to the center and does 25 merkins
PAX runs 25 yds to the south and does 25 BigBoys
PAX runs 25 yds to the center and does 25 merkins
PAX runs 30 yds to the east and does 25 curls
PAX runs 30 yds to the center and does 25 merkins

Once 45 minutes is finished the PAX shall immediately halt.

The QSource does not prescribe any particular religion, but rather that a man must have some kind of belief system to Accelerate his Faith. By Belief System, we mean the conviction that there is a supernatural governing force outside of oneself that provides an ordered explanation for our existence and delivers consequences for the violation of that order.
In support of that contention, let’s recall a few core concepts of the QSource. A Leader is a person who is able to influence other people to Move to Advantage. Movement is action taken to further Purpose, and Advantage is a superior circumstance achieved by that Movement. Leaders are Disruptive in that they cause a disturbance to a Group’s Status Quo by first visualizing an Advantage and then articulating it to the Group’s Members so persuasively that they begin to Move toward it.

The more skillful a Leader is at visualizing, articulating and persuading, the more Movement he will initiate in the Group and the more Effective he will be. However, this says nothing about his character. Ideally, he would also be a person who possesses Virtue, a standard of moral excellence. Unfortunately, this ideal combination of Virtue and Effectiveness is rare in one person. The un-Virtuous Leader is much more common. For every Lincoln there are ten Stalins who, while Effective, lack a Belief System that defines their character and provides boundaries to the dispensation of the power that is incumbent with their position.

BODEGA then water

Thus the dilemma that besets every Group: the more Effective its Leader is, the more power he will accumulate and the more likely it is that he will abuse it–absent some kind of restraint. As a result, in the fashioning of their worldly governing structures, Groups have continually sought to balance the need for Leaders who can successfully influence Movement to Advantage with the tendency of Effective Leaders to abuse the power they acquire in doing so.

The United States Constitution, which speaks directly to the separation and balancing of power, is a successful example of this attempt to both empower and restrain Leadership. Yet it’s not perfect, as no worldly structure can be. Regardless of their conceptual brilliance, to un-Virtuous Leaders overcome by the elixir of power, constitutional restraints are nothing but speed bumps on the road down which they are determined to drive their Groups–for bad or good.
True restraint doesn’t come from worldly structures. The only proven buffer to a Leader’s temptation to abuse his power comes from Virtue, and that is not self-generated. It is a result of character formed through adherence to a Belief System. Absent that, a Leader will make up his own rules because he has the power to do so. He will become corrupt, because that is what power (unrestrained by Guardrails) does to a man.

Prayer is the Pro’s antidote to anxiety
All men are subject to the emotions of fear and worry. In proper measure, they are an important part of the bundle of instincts that protect us from danger. Fear keeps us clear of the lion and worry spurs us to teach our sons to do the same. As such, fear and worry are necessary for self-preservation. But, like all good things, fear and worry can become so excessive that they interfere with our daily lives. They can take over. At that point, our emotions have reached a state of anxiety and anxiety is a Jester that hinders Acceleration.
A man has four options when anxiety threatens to overwhelm him. He can 1) surrender to it; 2) confront the emotion himself; 3) seek help in battling it from another man; or 4) Pray.

Option one doesn’t work at all. Men who surrender to anxiety as a permanent condition of their lives are the Amateurs who end up as Mascots with their boats capsized in the river. They cannot hope to be Right. At best, they can only do their best to seem Right.

Option two is only marginally better. Unlike the surrendering Mascot, the man who confronts his anxiety by himself has at least joined the battle. However, he is unlikely to succeed. Anxiety is a powerful emotion. How can a man alone be sure that his fear and worry is not warranted by his circumstances? Maybe the lion really is at his door. A man alone cannot provide himself with the objective counsel required to determine whether his emotions have crossed the line from healthy self-preservation into unhealthy anxiety.

Option three, seeking help from another man to battle anxiety, is far better. It is a major Advantage arising from the Shield Lock–one may be overpowered, but two can defend themselves. However, if that is all a man does then he is still acting like an Amateur rather than a Pro because he will continue to try to Control his anxiety rather than getting ready for it through Preparedness. To truly overcome anxiety, he must also Pray.

Hope is not self-generated. It starts with a firm belief that some force outside of oneself is directing Events and that the force has our best interests in mind. MAMMON- The Sustaining Relationship Between A Man And His Work. We are all created to perform some function for the betterment of those with whom we live in Proximity- Home, Fellowship, Community
Work is a Virtue- Men earn their daily bread through the sweat of their labor
Man’s relationship with his work, and the priority he makes it, must be in right order. If it’s not, it will swallow up/dominate his other relationships. 
There are three reasons for this:
1. Mammon Is The Easiest Relationship To Maintain- Mammon is limited in both time and scope. No other relationship is. Marriage and children are 24/7/365. Marriage & kids aren’t easy. Work, by comparison, is. 
2. Mammon Provides The Most Direct Affirmation- raises & promotions may affirm us.  A man never looks in the mirror and say “dang, I’m a good husband”? Clear & overt affirmation is rare, if not non-existent, in marriage & parenting. The clear feedback of the workplace tempts a man to turn away from the chaos and uncertainty of his life as a husband and father in favor of the easy and direct affirmation provided by Mammon.
3. Mammon Is The Only Relationship That Is Terminable At Will- Career selfishness is not only accepted, it’s a bit of cultural sin if not practiced. But a man cannot separate from his wife or kids without great difficulty and pain.
Mammon is a man’s least important relationship- The HIM must always keep the following in mind:
– If he places work before his M and Shorties he has committed relationship malpractice–and risks losing them
– If he places work before his Shield Lock (Fellowship) and his Blades the Community will suffer and erode–ultimately it will fall prey to what lurks outside the walls.                                                                                                                
– If he loses his family and his Community to his work, there is nothing for his work to sustain– Mammon is least important
Because it is easy, affirming and controllable, the temptation to elevate the importance of Mammon is compelling. The HIM recognizes this temptation for the Jester it is and resists it. Through Preparedness he keeps Mammon in its proper place at the outer ring of his Concentrica. The HIM may love his work, but he does not live to work. Instead, he works to enrich the lives of those he loves and with whom he lives.

1. Is there anything inherently good about work?
- Yes. Work provides stability for ourselves, our families, and our communities. The desire to work brings people together. The work we do as men in F3, for F3, drives us as well. QSOURCE 1.9 Mammon

Because a man’s connection with his work is so powerful, it has the potential to swallow up all his other relationships and move to the center of the Concentrica.

There are 3 reasons for this:

1. The Mammon relationship is easy. It has a set scope and duration. Punch in, punch out. We can’t take time off from being a father when a 2.0 is sick or punch out at the end of a marriage shift. Those relationships are constant.

2. Mammon provides direct affirmation. Do well, get a raise or a promotion. We are not given annual performance reviews by our Shieldlocks, and our Blades don’t offer us merit raises for being a good Stone.

3. A man’s relationship with his Mammon is terminable at will. At any time he can walk away from his job for any reason. Not so with his other relationships, some can never be terminated, but all require far more effort to end than that of his Mammon.

Q Source Topics

1. Is there anything inherently good about work?
- Yes. Work provides stability for ourselves, our families, and our communities. The desire to work brings people together. The work we do as men in F3, for F3, drives us as well. The passion to show up and support the men to your left and right, creating events to bring us together, opening up to each other, is all work for the betterment of us all.

2. Is work anything more than something we do?
- You can use both directions on this. You can say that it is just a means to support the family, a means to maintain your focus in life, or a mix of both. It is about balance and making sure that you do not live to work. Working to live and support your family should be the goal.

3. What priority should a man give to his work?
- I believe that the work everyone puts in their careers, hobbies, communities, and even F3 can be impactful for everyone, but does not take a priority to the family. Q Source Topics

1. Is there anything inherently good about work?
- Yes. Work provides stability for ourselves, our families, and our communities. The desire to work brings people together. The work we do as men in F3, for F3, drives us as well. The passion to show up and support the men to your left and right, creating events to bring us together, opening up to each other, is all work for the betterment of us all.

2. Is work anything more than something we do?
- You can use both directions on this. You can say that it is just a means to support the family, a means to maintain your focus in life, or a mix of both. It is about balance and making sure that you do not live to work. Working to live and support your family should be the goal.

3. What priority should a man give to his work?
- I believe that the work everyone puts in their careers, hobbies, communities, and even F3 can be impactful for everyone, but does not take priority to the family. This can be difficult to manage due to needing a break, and stressful times at home, but cannot become the norm or else you may lose what you've built.

Mammon Is The Easiest Relationship To Maintain
Unlike the other relationships on the HIM’s Concentrica, Mammon is limited in both time and scope. All jobs have a time-clock of sorts to punch. No job is 24/7. When a man leaves work for the day, he may keep thinking about it but he does not have to interact with it. He can take vacations from it. He can call in sick if he must. Do any of these time limitations apply to any of his other relationships? Can he punch out on his marriage for the night? Can he take a vacation from his children? Not really. Those relationships are all encompassing. There is no such thing as off-duty if your child is sick. Nor is there any limitation on the scope of a man’s duties as husband and father. A good boss will give you a clear job description so that you know what is expected of you. As a husband and father, you won’t need anything like that because everything is expected of you. Of all the relationships on the Concentrica, Mammon is the easiest to maintain

Q Source Topics

1. Is there anything inherently good about work?
- Yes. Work provides stability for ourselves, our families, and our communities. The desire to work brings people together. The work we do as men in F3, for F3, drives us as well. The passion to show up and support the men to your left and right, creating events to bring us together, opening up to each other, is all work for the betterment of us all.

2. Is work anything more than something we do?
- You can use both directions on this. You can say that it is just a means to support the family, a means to maintain your focus in life, or a mix of both. It is about balance and making sure that you do not live to work. Working to live and support your family should be the goal.

3. What priority should a man give to his work?
- I believe that the work everyone puts in their careers, hobbies, communities, and even F3 can be impactful for everyone, but does not take a priority to the family. Q source Whetstone
Like the Shield Lock, the Whetstone is a relationship that is subject to the 3P: it must be Proximate, Purposeful and Periodic to be Effective. 

– Proximity requires the Stone to physically meet with his Blade. While it is fine (good even) for them to also talk on the telephone and email, that is not a replacement for the physical meeting where they can look each other in the eye. Hard looks and straight talk (tempered by love) get results. That cannot be done virtually. 

– To be Purposeful, the meeting between the Stone and the Blade must be more than the kind of inconsequential pizza party a Club would have–it must have a particular Outcome in mind: the Acceleration of the Blade’s Preparedness.  Just as a Workout should Accelerate the HIM’s Fitness, the Whetstone should Accelerate the Blade’s proper personal alignment. 

– There is no set rule for the periodic regularity of the meeting between the Stone and the Blade. It must be frequent enough to be Effective but not so frequent that the Stone and Blade smother each other. This is something both men must determine through trial and error. However, because it is (by design) a Movement away from the Status Quo it will cause pain, and it is man’s general hardwiring to avoid pain. As a result, the Stone must be deliberate to ensure regular meetings. Otherwise, his Blade will drift away to something easier.

Q source Whetstone
Like the Shield Lock, the Whetstone is a relationship that is subject to the 3P: it must be Proximate, Purposeful and Periodic to be Effective. 

– Proximity requires the Stone to physically meet with his Blade. While it is fine (good even) for them to also talk on the telephone and email, that is not a replacement for the physical meeting where they can look each other in the eye. Hard looks and straight talk (tempered by love) get results. That cannot be done virtually. 

– To be Purposeful, the meeting between the Stone and the Blade must be more than the kind of inconsequential pizza party a Club would have–it must have a particular Outcome in mind: the Acceleration of the Blade’s Preparedness. The Stone’s task within the Whetstone is to help the Blade get ready for the expected and be ready for the unexpected by both encouraging him to turn Pro and providing him with the Bricks he will need to build his own Guardrails. Just as a Workout should Accelerate the HIM’s Fitness, the Whetstone should Accelerate the Blade’s proper personal alignment. 

– There is no set rule for the periodicity of the meeting between the Stone and the Blade. It must be frequent enough to be Effective but not so frequent that the Stone and Blade smother each other. This is something both men must determine through trial and error. However, because it is (by design) a Movement away from the Status Quo it will cause pain, and it is man’s general hardwiring to avoid pain. As a result, the Stone must be deliberate to ensure periodicity. Otherwise, his Blade will drift away to something easier.

The Vertical Relationship Between Men
A man must be sharpened like a knife blade
Both a man and a knife are made to cut, but neither can be Effective until properly honed.
A knife is sharpened by a whetstone. While water is used to lubricate the whetstone prior to sharpening that is not where the “whet” part comes from. To whet actually means to sharpen, like with a man’s appetite and his curiosity. In other words, to whet both blade and man is to put on an edge, with a result that is sharp, dynamic and ready to cut. The unsharpened man is dull and lethargic, in-Effective as a Leader and ill-Prepared for the Obstacles he will face in his life.
Just as a man’s appetite for pure food must be whetted, so must his appetite for the heavy responsibility that comes with Leadership . The HIM acts as the Stone to the younger man’s Blade , providing the hard surface against which he becomes sharper and whetting his appetite for greater responsibility.

Like the Shield Lock, the Whetstone is a relationship that is subject to the 3P: it must be Proximate, Purposeful and periodic to be Effective.
– Proximity requires the Stone to physically meet with his Blade. While it is fine (good even) for them to also talk on the telephone and email, that is not a replacement for the physical meeting where they can look each other in the eye. Hard looks and straight talk (tempered by love) get results. That cannot be done virtually.
– To be Purposeful, the meeting between the Stone and the Blade must be more than the kind of inconsequential pizza party a Club would have–it must have a particular Outcome in mind: the Acceleration of the Blade’s Preparedness. The Stone’s task within the Whetstone is to help the Blade get ready for the expected and be ready for the unexpected by both encouraging him to turn Pro and providing him with the Bricks he will need to build his own Guardrails. Just as a Workout should Accelerate the HIM’s Fitness, the Whetstone should Accelerate the Blade’s proper personal alignment.
– There is no set rule for the periodicity of the meeting between the Stone and the Blade. It must be frequent enough to be Effective but not so frequent that the Stone and Blade smother each other. This is something both men must determine through trial and error. However, because it is (by design) a Movement away from the Status Quo it will cause pain, and it is man’s general hardwiring to avoid pain. As a result, the Stone must be deliberate to ensure periodicity. Otherwise, his Blade will drift away to something easier.

YHC revealed some super original wisdom by providing a proverb that I came up with that goes: "Fall down 7, Stand up 8" (R) Trademark and Patent Pending. Feel free to pass along to your Blades -- just give credit where credit is due.

But seriously for anyone not familiar with the old Japanese or Chinese (pretty sure not knowing the difference is offensive, sorry guys) it basically is a reminder that no matter how many times you fall, what matters is that you keep getting back up.

We would advance together as a group, we would fall together as a group, we would get up together as a group, we would do WORK together as a group (because this is the 2nd thing you do when you fall, first you STAND UP up, then second you DO THE WORK so you won't fall again, and then you go FORWARD), so we go forward again and fall again (because we are humans and this is what we do) as a group and then repeato until we get to last cone (Number 7). Thang 1 - AMRAP for Autism

This is the inaugural AMRAP for Autism for F3 Aggieland.

Here are some facts that I think you should know about Autism Spectrum Disorder, otherwise known as ASD.

1. Autism spectrum disorder affects 1 in 36 children.
2. Boys are nearly 5 times more likely than girls to be diagnosed with ASD.  Girls are often underdiagnosed with autism and misdiagnosed with other conditions.
3. Autism spectrum disorder is one of the fastest-growing developmental disorders in the United States. ASD is more common than childhood cancer, diabetes, and AIDS combined.
4. Autism spectrum disorder affects all nationalities, all creeds, all religions, all races and both sexes. It doesn’t differentiate or affect only one group.
5. Autism spectrum disorder is a developmental disability that often presents with challenges before the age of 3 and lasts throughout a person’s lifetime.
6. Early identification, treatment, and support matters! Many important outcomes for children's lives are significantly improved with early diagnosis and treatment.
7. Many individuals with autism spectrum disorder have difficulties with communication. For some people this can look like significant challenges with spoken language and for others it can look like challenges with social communication.
8. Autism spectrum disorder is not a disorder that gets worse with age. Individuals with ASD can learn and build new skills with the right support, and are most likely to improve with specialized, individualized services and opportunities for supported inclusion.
9. Some famous names that have been diagnosed with ASD include Elon Musk, Lionel Messi, Eminem, Bill Gates, Temple Grandin, Dan Akroyd, Daryl Hannah, Tim Burton and Albert Einstein.
10. There’s a saying in the Autism community that says “If you've met one person with autism, you've met one person with autism." Individuals diagnosed with ASD present with unique strengths and difficulties and experience characteristics of their disability in different ways.

Now for the exercises.

Since 1 in every 36 kids are diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder, we are going to do 36 reps of 5 different exercises. Once you complete all five exercises, you will run a lap around the senior center. Everything is OYO.

Man hunts best in a pack

Eyes to the side have the animals that hide. Eyes up front have the animals that hunt.

Man’s eyes are up front. We are hunters not hiders. In fact, we are the apex predator of the Earth’s apex predators. But unlike the other hunters, our success is not based upon strength, speed or the size of our fangs. It is our ability to hunt together in a very complex way that puts man at the very top of the food chain. No other animal can do that.

Some animals, like wolves, do hunt in packs because they have evolved to be more successful that way. But their focus is solely on their prey, what they can see before them with their eyes up front. When they claim their prey it is distributed along a vertical pecking order starting with the alpha male of the pack.

The man-pack hunts differently. Instead of focusing solely on his prey, a man also works cooperatively with other men in the pack to see what might be behind him. He recognizes that his eyes up front can only see from 9 through 12 to 3 o’clock. He is blind to his Six unless another man watches it for him. After all, what good is the hunt if the hunter himself is taken by something that sneaks up on him from a place that he, by himself, cannot observe? No man can see his own Six.

The HIM’s relationship with his children is unique in a critical way. It is the one connection that can never be fully severed. He can quit his job and get a new one. He can divorce his wife and remarry. But every child he has remains his child forever regardless of how far he may roam, how distant he may become or how many other children he may have. Even after he has left the Earth his children will rely throughout their lives upon him as the centering anchor empowering them to move boldly without fear of being cast loose from Virtue.
The HIM’s unwavering sacrifice for his children allows them the freedom to grow into the men and women they were created to be. He bears this in mind in all his works and efforts.

1. What can a father hold back from his children?
 - The answer is usually nothing at all. We give everything that we have into our kids so they can have it better than we did/the best that we can provide. 1. What can a father hold back from his children?
- The answer is usually nothing at all. We give everything that we have into our kids so they can have it better than we did/the best that we can provide. 2. How important is a father?
- A father is one of the most important figures to a 2.0. Your reactions and actions carry the most weight with your 2.0's because that's how they learn how to act. You will mess up and get too angry, curse, say something you regret, etc and that's okay. You are meant to fail. No one is perfect and it's impossible to emulate that and set impossible standards for your 2.0's

3. Why must a father be strong for his children?
- As I stated earlier, you are the one they will look up to to know what is right and wrong. You will fail, but your true strength will be how you react when you mess up. Will you deflect, or will you own your mistakes and me that role model that 2.0 already believes you to be?

The Sacrificial Relationship Between A Man And His Children
A man gives everything he has for his children
After the M, Shorties are next on the next ring on the Concentrica. The HIM’s relationship with his children is sacrificial because he will give up everything he has for them. How much money does he spend on each of his children? Simple: all the money he has divided by the number of children he is raising.

The HIM’s relationship with his children is unique in a critical way. It is the one connection that can never be fully severed. He can quit his job and get a new one. He can divorce his wife and remarry. But every child he has remains his child forever regardless of how far he may roam, how distant he may become or how many other children he may have. A man may depart from his children, but he cannot quit them. While he may hide from them physically or emotionally his responsibility for them is eternal, as will be the consequences if commits relationship malpractice in their upbringing. The seeds of discontent sown by the ineffective father will yield a legacy of damaged fruit.

The IMPACT (for good or bad) that a man has on his children cannot be underestimated
The quality of a man’s relationship with his children defines the quality of their relationships with everyone else for the rest of their lives. If he is absent, they will be distrustful. If he is capricious, they will be unjust. If he is cold, they will be withdrawn. But, if he is present, just and warm the HIM will have imprinted upon his children’s hearts a template of relational success upon which they can rely throughout their lives. They will in turn pass it on to their Shorties. In this way, the IMPACT is infinite.

The HIM’s Commitment provides his children freedom
A father is to his children as the needle point of a compass is to the pencil. As they grow, the arc of their lives is naturally drawn further and further away from the center. The HIM founds his point in deep and solid rock, knowing this will ensure that the progressively enlarging circles his children draw will remain true. Even after he has left the Earth his children will rely throughout their lives upon him as the centering anchor empowering them to move boldly without fear of being cast loose from Virtue.


The HIM’s unwavering sacrifice for his children allows them the freedom to grow into the men and women they were created to be. He bears this in mind in all his works and efforts.


For them, he sacrifices everything

How quickly your heart returns to its regular resting rate following exercise is measured by heart rate recovery . So, how to improve heart recovery rate?


This measurement is used by some health and fitness experts to gauge the heart’s capacity to recover after strenuous exercise.


This article discusses the significance of heart rate recovery, how to measure it, and suggestions for how to improve heart recovery rate. How quickly your heart returns to its regular resting rate following exercise is measured by heart rate recovery.
What Is Heart Rate Recovery?


Your heart rate recovery may have come up in a fitness class or personal training session you attended. Heart rate recovery differs from your target heart rate, which is the heart rate you want to reach while exercising, and your average resting heart rate (your heart rate when you have not been doing any activity).


The change in your heart rate for the first few minutes following exercise is measured by your recovery heart rate. It is often determined in the first one to three minutes following activity. Your post-workout heart rate is another name for heart rate recovery.


In general, your heart will recover from activity more quickly the more physically fit you are.
Why Heart Rate Recovery Matters?

Because it can be used to understand how the heart recovers from stress, heart rate recovery is significant.


Stress on the body is purposely and safely increased through exercise. Exercise-induced stress aids in the maintenance of strong muscles, lungs, and cardiovascular (heart and blood vessel) health.


If your heart doesn’t bounce back quickly from exercise, this could indicate a lack of fitness or even significant health issues.


According to research published in 2017, following exercise, a slower heart rate decline increased the risk of conditions like:
Heart condition
Diabetes (chronic condition affecting how your body uses glucose, or sugar)
Persistent inflammation
Chest pain (when blood flow to the heart is blocked)
Stroke (when blood flow to the brain is interrupted or reduced)
Abnormal heartbeat


Many healthcare practitioners utilise heart rate recovery to forecast illness risk and risk of death from heart disease due to its significance to fitness level and cardiovascular health.
How To Monitor Your Recovery Heart Rate?
Wear a heart rate monitor or place your hand over the sensors on an aerobic workout machine that measure your heart rate.
10 to 20 minutes of easy exercise.
Check your peak heart recovery rate after your exercise session. This is the peak number of heartbeats you experienced during the exercise session.
Then, keep track of or write down how long it takes your heart rate to drop by 10, 20, or even 30 beats.
Always keep in mind that a quicker healing time is preferable, and regular exercise will help you get there.
Factors That Affect Your Heart Recovery Rate


Your heart recovery rate is influenced by more than simply your level of general fitness. Therefore, it’s crucial to comprehend how these components impact heart rate recovery in order to watch changes in it.
Fatigue
Caffeine
Dehydration
Fatigue


Your heart is affected by fatigue and lack of sleep, among other bodily organs. According to research, exhaustion affects the peak heart rate and post-exercise heart recovery rate.
Caffeine


The neurological system is stimulated by caffeine, which can hinder the body’s capacity to recuperate from exercise. According to a 2017 study, caffeine consumption impairs the recovery of blood pressure and heart rate after exercise.
Dehydration


It’s critical to have enough water in your system for a healthy physique. According to research, dehydration can increase heart rate and modify how the heart works. Lack of water might also make it harder for your heart to recover after exercise.
How To Improve Heart Recovery Rate


Here are some other suggestions how to improve heart recovery rate or to help you become more physically active and fit:
Go up the stairs.
Park further from the entrance.
Intensify exercises gradually.
Enroll in group exercise sessions.
Make use of a personal trainer.
Take a stroll with a companion.
Work in the yard or garden.
Organize your home.
Test out various workout formats.


You might be asking how to enhance heart recovery rate now that you are aware of it. First, be sure to take into account any other circumstances, such as insufficient sleep, coffee use, and dehydration, that could affect how quickly your heart rate recovers.


These variables may affect how accurate the figures are while measuring changes in your heart recovery rate. Physical activity is the most crucial element for enhancing your healing heart recovery rate.


If the idea of exercising more and becoming more active overcomes you, remember that it doesn’t have to be a significant shift. Your fitness levels will improve even with little activity improvements. Instead of focusing on creating an impossible goal, consider about starting where you are.


Start by adding one or two quick walks each day if you are currently sedentary. Then gradually lengthen the time you spend moving. Even simple tasks like vacuuming, sweeping, or using a push mower to trim the lawn count toward your daily exercise.
What Is A Good Heart Rate?


One of the numbers you may monitor to assess your fitness and health progress is average heart rate recovery. Some people track their heart rates throughout the day and during physical activity. How do you determine if your stats are healthy, though? What is a healthy heartbeat?


Your heart rate is influenced by a wide range of circumstances. If it fluctuates during the day between the average and yours, it could be caused by heat, caffeine use, genetics, emotions, body position, or medications. Generally speaking, as your level of fitness increases and your cardiovascular system becomes more effective, your daily heart rate will decrease.


Typically, a average heart rate recovery ranges from 60 to 100 beats per minute. Generally speaking, a lower heart rate (within that range) is preferred.


How quickly your average heart rate recovery to a resting level is measured by average heart rate recovery. Your overall cardiovascular health and degree of fitness can be evaluated using your recovery heart rate.


You can use a monitor or a manual test to see if your heart rate recovers. For instance, if you relax for one minute and your heart rate reduces by 15 beats per minute, your average heart rate recovery is 15.


The most crucial element affecting your average heart rate recovery is your level of fitness, but it’s also impacted by exhaustion, coffee use, and water intake.

A- As you get fitter, your heart will recover more quickly. A score of 25 to 30 beats per minute for recovery is considered good, and a score of 50 to 60 beats per minute is regarded as exceptional.

OFFICIAL BACK BLAST OF 2024

An idea…then to a plan…then to witnessing 11 badass HIMS take on a revolutionary challenge. Rucking what has only been ran. The Texas Independence Relay. 

Team 1 (in order)
1) Pi 3.14 30.08 miles
2) YHC Zelda 39.36 miles
3) Fuego 32.11 miles 
4) Turnbuckle 30.24 miles
5) Big Short 29.95 miles
6) faceplant 33.43 miles

Team 2 (in order)
1) Bunker 14.85 miles
2) SnoopDog 19.12 miles
3) Vibram! 18.54 miles
4) Ewok 16.28 miles
5) Cold Turkey 14.17 miles 

As Team 1 arrived to Gonzales on a cool 58° Friday morning, one can only describe the city as a ghost town. With a slight fog in the air, the 10am hour was upon us and while there was no cannon shot, our step off was just as monumental as any other!

With the badass himself Pi 3.14 taking the holeshot, spirits were high, and a LFG attitude was radiating off all the PAX.  Pi 3.14 even managed to get chased, attacked, a bitten by a ferocious dog (chihuahua lol) but continued on cause NCWH! 

Leg after leg came and went and with Fuego breaking off a 13:55 pace, before we knew it, nightfall was upon us.
With fatigue setting in, communication lacking, and testosterone flaring, we began asking ourselves “can we really do this for 2 nights and 3 days?”. None the less, we trucked on and with a new sunrise came a new LFG attitude! Saturday was a breath of fresh air as our fellowship grew, our motivation was found, and before we knew it, EVERY PAX was rucking sub 14. Yes, we found ourselves pacing 2 HOURS ahead of schedule just 24 hours into our 52 hour event, so the team was told to slow down as we did not want to reach St Arnold’s at 0600 😂. PAX did not wanna hear “slow down”…. So the ever so hardheaded Turnbuckle rucked at a 16:29 pace instead of the prescribed 16:30 LOL
Night 2 came and went, and will little rest, we were soon at the FINAL LEG. With each PAX having just 1 ruck left, the afterburners were engaged and who would have thought, we saw our FIRST RUNNER Sunday at 0615!

With Big Short rucking his 6TH LEG at a 14:25 pace (yall, this man is 69 years old, WTF?!), he handed off to faceplant for the 36th and final leg and at 12:19pm, the rest of Team 1 joined as the first ever TIR rucking team crossed that finish line. 


From Team 2 Captain Vibram!:

@Zelda leading this project did the setup and order (leg assignment).
In a brush of luck and faith I picked up the phone and called a few ruckers that I have on speed dial and SnoopDog said, yeah man sounds stupid, sign me up; I have to give this HIM major props because we met back in July 2020 in a launch and we have been good friends since then, he currently lives in San Antonio and of course, drove in to attack this CSAUP w/us! 

As voluntold Team 2 capitano, I had no idea of the rucking capabilities outside Snoop and YHC, so I resorted to having zero expectations (in a good way) from the other 3 PAX.

We had a few meetings but they were a bit hit a miss, I have never met this Cold Turkey guy, Bunker I remember he bought a plate from me and he had to remind me a few times that we had met before and no idea who this Ewok  guy until in a face to face meeting it took me like 20 mins going through my rolodex to realize I was his proud papa LMAO; he was walking his dog while we were doing at The Arena and I kept calling him out “quit looking at us and just join in the fun”……he did in the last set of Merkins and came out later and started posting.

Leading to this event, we had a Team 2 meeting on Thursday night (36 hrs to STARTEX) and right after the call, both Cold Turkey  and Ewok  did not have Ruck+Plate for the event…….I thought to my self: this weekend is either gonna be really short or really interesting!

At this point I tried my best to not flood my head w/doubts outside of my own self doubts, I already was thinking to myself: am I prepared for this? Can I lead by example? Fear of failure was lurking, a demon that I have been trying to shake off for the better part of last 6 months.

I told these guys in the chat that I was bringing a Ruck ready to go and they sourced the 2nd one, so by 24 hrs to startex we all had our rucks ready to go!

Our original assignment:
Cannon blast 0830 from Gonzalez, TX
Ruck legs 1 through 5 
“Split” and jump to legs 11 through 15 ending in Weimer, TX
“Split” and go “rest” to restart at Good Times at 0800 Sunday starting at leg 31 

Saturday 0430 we meet, load the van and head out to Gonzalez!

We melt the ice fast and start 2nd Fing (read out loud a few times and starts sounding wrong) right away, we get to destination and we already feel we have been knowing each other for years, the jokes go “off the reservation” many times and we have to “reel it back in” constantly; every time we were in the van it turned into “super-duper-COT” (but not like the Austin “pride” team van offering BJs for $1.25 and not free due to inflation)

We had a cannon blast at 0830 and Bunker started our 1st cluster of legs!
At this time I am still into the “no expectation” zone but keeping in touch w/Team 1 that started 22 hrs before us and averaging 14 min/miles (in rucking terms, this is a great pace, although for all FTX TIR running teams you need 7 min/mile pace for them to start talking to you).

NOTE:
For those that don’t know a leisure rucking pace (w/at least 30-45lb wt) is 20 min/mile so if you can do a bit of math, this is would put you at the 3 mile/hr pace depending on what kind of conspiracy theorist you are of course; so when the FTX boys get chubbies when they hear of a PAX that can sustain 7 to sub 7 min/mile pace for 6 to 7 miles, the rucking community will bobble their heads like our Indian brothers when we hear that someone like Fuego can ruck 14 min/mile carryin 60 lbs and say, NCWH or “nobody cares what you can do fresh” and other shit talking phrases, but what we really mean is / damn that’s a really good pace!

So we all finish our 1st leg w/great pace and feeling really good, doing our split into leg 11! 

We all do our 2nd leg and we get to Weimer, TX at 22:00 and start planning what to do, are going to rest or go meet w/team 1 or what?

We decide, this is a CSAUP, let’s get some food and meet w/the other team and decide when to step off from Good Times Running.

We make a stop at Denny’s in Brookshire (the ‘shire” and of course I get, not “a ton” but 3 tons of shit from my pronunciation inside the “super-duper COT mobile”, I call pronounce it “Dennis” so there you have it……..thanks Bunker  🙄

We make it to Good Times Running and the consensus is: take a short nap and we start back again, we may finish by noon and we can go back to our concentrica earlier!

We stepped off at 0240, this was the only leg we did as a unit, Pi 3.14 and Bunker side-by side (no they did not hold hands).
Due to our experiment of being the Guinea pigs and testing it to possibly opening the TIR Rucking division in 2025 (we as Team 2 did this as a 5 man team from the start because we could not find a 6th -your loss-) and due to the time of the day, the access to support vehicles was closed for this leg (#32) we made the exec decision to skip this leg, although my hat is off to @Zelda for
Kicking this leg’s ass, later we found out that the leg was pretty flooded, SnoopDog took the last leg to bring us home and we made it work out.

We all finished our 3rd leg and headed out to St. Arnold’s (I possibly mispronounce this one as well), we all ruck up and went 1/4 mile back tracking the last leg to meet w/SnoopDog

We all finished whole, we had a lot of
fun and pretty confident that the TIR organizers would consider opening a Rucking division w/our AAR, but if you know me, IDKS.

HIM has many relationships in his concentrica that he works to accelerate. 
Relationship with self or fitness is one element and only requires one direction of acceleration. It is one sided and not overly dynamic. Next comes the relationships with friends/other men/PAx. This can be a little more tedious and fluctuate while we attempt to accelerate and balance the plates we have spinning. There is weight on either side and the HIM fights for balance. A HIM prepares for the expected and is ready for the unexpected. He controls himself to better control his relationships and so on. These relationships do not take a back seat to a HIMs work, though we often misprioritize the levels of concentrica. Next break we talk about the bullseye, the M.

The M is the most important relationship. She is at the bullseye of the concentrica. HIM has a finite amount of time represented by arrows in a quiver and is very conscientious when he takes aim at his concentrica. Q Source (M Relationship - aka marriage)
Intentional
Make time/space and be intentional about investing in your relationship with your M. Be genuinely engaged and interested in her as a person. Ask her questions about herself, how she's doing and what is going on in her life. We all change constantly and continuing to know your M takes constant effort, not to mention it makes her feel loved and seen. Learn to communicate with your M, and if that means that you have to seek outside help to do so then make that happen. There is no shame in needing help to sort through your communication struggles as a couple. 
Happiness vs Joy/Contentment
Our culture feeds us that lie that one of the purposes of marriage is happiness but that untruth will poison your marriage. According to my beliefs our marriages call us to a higher purpose. We are to love our Ms the same way that Jesus loved the Church when he became human, put aside his own comfort, placed the needs of his "bride" above his own desires and ultimately gave up his life for "her." (Ephesians 5:22-33) That's the mark that we are aiming for and while unattainable, that purpose will continually refine us.
Not 50/50
Instead of being concerned about equal efforts in our M relationships we should be concerned about aligned efforts. The goal is that you and your M are on the same page and both putting 100% effort into achieving your aligned goals. In different seasons each of you will shoulder more of that load than the other, but always complimenting and supporting each other. Our calling as the leader in this space is to always show up and always put in the work. Investing time in and having your 3Fs right sure makes this a lot easier to do. Notice I didn't say our calling is to be perfect. This is a "till death do us part process" and you will fail at times. Be quick to own it, apologize and find a way to move forward.

Q Source Topics
1. Is work-life balance a useful concept?
- Yes and no. Life is about balance, but that balance is a rollercoaster where sometimes you have to focus more on work/less on relationships and vice versa. The key to finding that balance is being prepared for busy seasons in your work life and in your relationship life.

2. Are some relationships more important than others?
- Yes. With your M. 100%. When you decided to marry your M, you agreed to become one with her. The two of y'all's actions and reactions are a reflection of each other now. Building your relationship with your M and making it a priority will improve you as well. Keep in mind that at the end of the day, the two of you are a team. Once you wed, she is no longer of her father's namesake, and even though you still maintain yours, you are separate from your parents, brothers, and sisters now. The team that the two of you form now, takes precedence over the rest.

3. Is meeting your wife halfway good enough?
- Never. You should always be looking to improve your relationship with your M. Comfortability in where y'all are at in your relationship leads to vulnerability to losing that connection. Yes, it is difficult to give 100% all the time, but making the effort to not give up is what will keep you progressing forward. Remember that there will be times that are tough that you will fail at. That's good. You need hard times to make your relationship stronger. Just do not give up on each other or yourself. My favorite quote that you will hear me say repeatedly is: “You have to pull an arrow back to shoot it forward.”

1. Is work-life balance a useful concept?
*Yes and no. Life is about balance, but that balance is a rollercoaster where sometimes you have to focus more on work/less on relationships and vice versa. The key to finding that balance is being prepared for busy seasons in your work life and in your relationship life.

2. Are some relationships more important than others?
*Yes. With your M. 100%. When you decided to marry your M, you agreed to become one with her. The two of y'all's actions and reactions are a reflection of each other now. Building your relationship with your M and making it a priority will improve you as well. Keep in mind that at the end of the day, the two of you are a team. Once you wed, she is no longer of her father's namesake, and even though you still maintain yours, you are separate from your parents, brothers, and sisters now. The team that the two of you form now, takes precedence over the rest.

3. Is meeting your wife halfway good enough?
*Never. You should always be looking to improve your relationship with your M. Comfortability in where y'all are at in your relationship leads to vulnerability to losing that connection. Yes, it is difficult to give 100% all the time, but giving the effort to not give up is what will keep you progressing forward. Remember that there will be times that are tough that you will fail. That's good. You need hard times to make your relationship stronger. Just do not give up on each other or yourself. My favorite quote that you will hear me say again and again is: “You have to pull an arrow back in order to shoot an arrow forward.”

THANG 1 - THE BEEP THANG (basically a modified PACER - Progressive Aerobic Cardiovascular Endurance Run - test)
Pax lineup along sideline of basketball court facing Rockingham Loop (YHC's house)
Pax will be continuously running from sideline to sideline (50 feet/15.24 meters) on pre recorded beeps.
Beeps initially start out 9 seconds apart on Level 1 and eventually narrowed down to 4.5 seconds between beeps at Level 17.
The time between recorded beeps decreases each level (approximately 1 minute) requiring an increase in pace.
The PAX continue until they are unable to keep pace with the beeps.

Once PAX is out, they go to sidewalk and perform the following:
- Freddy Mercuries - 10 (2 is 1)
- Mountain Climbers - 10 (2 is 1)
- 10 count (Not gonna lie, I took my 10 count before doing Freddy Ms)
- Repeat until all PAX are eliminated by beeps

Q Source: The Jester
A HIM gets ready for the expected and stays ready for the unexpected. How he does this depends on the man and his unique Jester. 

Likewise, if my relationship with those in Proximity and my Creator are not Right and Accelerating, then I am more vulnerable to temptation from new and unexpected circumstances.
While I can never out-paddle my Jester, the faster my boat is Accelerating through the water the harder it is for him to capsize it.

Obviously, the Jester is Satan, lack of self-discipline and the temptations into which we are led. 

Thankfully, we can rejoice because Scripture tells us this:
“No temptation has overtaken you but such as is common to man; and God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will provide the way of escape also, so that you will be able to endure it.” 1 Corinthians 10:13

And in this truth we know that other men are going through the same thing that we are, so we’d be fools NOT to lean on each other for help and encouragement. 

If you are at war with sin, you are at peace with Christ, conversely if you are at war with Christ, you’re at peace with sin. Fight the right battle. Fight the jester, the liar, the tempter.

5 Lies of the Jester 
Luckily for us, while the Jester is a devious liar, he is not that creative. Regardless of the type of temptation, his lies fall into a discernible pattern and always have, for nothing changes under the sun. Here are the five biggest lies the Jester has told since time began:
1. You Are The Boss Of Me. The Jester is a parasite whose ultimate objective is sovereignty over his host. Because no man will knowingly and willingly cede his freedom, the Jester tells us not to believe our lying eyes as we gradually lose control. “You” the Jester promises “can stop me anytime you want. You just say the word, and I’ll be gone.” The Jester keeps whispering this lie until the day the he need speak it no more.
2. You Are What You Do. We were created for far better things than the dirty life our Jester would have us lead. Those better things are what man calls Virtue , and they are baked into our hearts from inception. When our Jester causes us to stumble, the result won’t square with our hard-wired need for Virtue. We rightly feel that what we have wrongly done is not who we are and seek to avoid doing it again. That is the precise moment that our Jester tells us the second lie: “no, it is not the Virtuous-self that is truly you, it is the stumbling-self. If you are Virtue, then why does stumbling come so easily to you? Why does it feel so natural? Isn’t it more likely that these things you do reflect who you really are? Who you were intended to be?” LIE!! That is a lie! We were not born to stumble, we are led to do so. We are not what we do but what we were intended to be.
3. You Are (relatively) Not That Bad A Guy. The Jester is slick. If we recognize that he is becoming the boss (and seek to resist him), and that what he would have us do is not who we are supposed to be, the Jester turns to one of the oldest tricks in his filthy book: moral relativism. “Sure” he concedes “this thing that you are may not be what was intended, I’ll give you that. But, is it really all that bad . . . on relative terms?” What the Jester intends is for us to turn our heads away from the mirror and look (down) upon the lives of our brothers, who (unlike us) are TRULY screwed up. Sure, I may be addicted to pornography, but at least I don’t smoke crack, like Bob! The Jester even gives us a ready-made Oprah Bomb for the occasion: “there, but for the grace of God walk I”. That is not in the Bible. It is only found in the Jester’s book of lies.
4. The Jester And Virtue Can Coexist. Have you ever heard your Jester ask you something like this: “aren’t the big good things you do more important than these tiny little bad things you and I occasionally do together?” By this lie, the Jester seeks to train us to say “yeah/but”, as in: YEAH I smoke some crack, BUT I do pay my child support on time. I guess I can do both as long as the good I do outweighs the bad. To help the Jester maintain this lie, we erect complex scoreboards for our lives in which our Jester seems to lose out to our Virtue by a respectable margin every time. It’s like Al Gore hiring a man to plant trees in Sri Lanka to offset the miles he flies back and forth to Vail in his private jet. F3 calls these Virtue Credits . They are worthless because they are unredeemable.
5. You Can’t Live, If Living Is Without Me. A man who breathes dirty air long enough forgets how sweet the pure stuff is. The Jester depends on our tendency to forget to convince us that we never knew a life without him. But we did know, we were born knowing and we can get back to it, but only if we see through this fifth lie which, at its heart, is that there is no hope. That is a lie. There is hope, there always is. The HIM is to be a purveyor of hope.

Weight control requires Accountability
First, let me acknowledge that not every man needs Accountability to maintain his ideal weight. Some men are ectomorphs who can’t gain weight even if they want to. Others are mesomorphs whose high metabolism turns extra calories into lean muscle. If you have either of those body types you can skip ahead to the next QPoint. Or, better yet, read this next section so you can help people in your Groups who fall into the third category: endomorphs.
Endomorphs are men  whose bellies make great body-fat storage units. Because I am an endomorph my body reacts quickly and predictably when I lose portion control. When I eat too much, I get fat regardless of how much I am exercising. While I yearn to be a mesomorph who can out-King his Queen I have come to accept that I never can–and recognize that the yearning itself is a gilded ticket for a free ride on the ferry boat of self-delusion. Trying to out-King my Queen leads me to abandon the daily discipline over what I put in my body, which leads me to get fat–every time I try it. The ferry boat only has one destination, and that is fat-guy island.

The truth is that I need help to resist accepting the golden ticket. I need the external enforcement mechanism of Accountability to maintain the Queen. And, ectomorphs and mesomorphs notwithstanding, so do the majority of other men.

Thing 2 
Move to tennis courts
Face the same way
Lunge forward long side
Al Gore shuffle short side
Back lunges long side
Al Gore shuffle short side

The first step in Queen/Accountability is to set a Standard. While that can be difficult in other areas of a man’s life, with the Queen it’s simple, it is his ideal weight and his ideal FUPA . These two measures are both objective and truthful. They don’t lie or coddle, they just deliver data. I know they work because whenever I take the golden ticket and try to out-King my Queen my first step is to abandon them in favor of the subjective untruthful “standards” of how I look and how I feel. The mirror and my feelings lie to me–they are the dock workers on the ferry boat of self-delusion. Their job is to get me on the boat. Listening to them is a mistake.
BODEGA

The second step is Enforcement, the external force that applies the Standard. That too is simple with Queen/Accountability, it starts with a daily weigh-in and FUPA-taping, what we call the LBZ . To be Effective, the LBZ has to be done at the same time every day (it doesn’t matter when, but first thing in the morning is best) with the same measurement devices. This takes out the fluctuations as much as possible.
For a highly disciplined man, the single Brick of the LBZ might be enough. For me, it’s not. I also need the second Brick of conveying the results of my LBZ to men to whom I have delegated the authority of Enforcement. They know (because I told them) that if I don’t convey my LBZ (or a legitimate reason why I couldn’t do so that day) then it is probable that I have accepted the golden ticket and am en-route to fat-guy island. If so, their job is simple. They are to grab me by the collar and yank me back to the dry ground of reality. The harder the yank and the closer I still am to the dock the better
BODEGA

The final step is Consequence, which is the result of Enforcement. If my LBZ pushes up above my ideal weight/FUPA I reduce my daily calories from net-2100 to net-1500 until I get back below it. Experience has shown me that net-1500 is where I lose weight. Your results may vary. Net-1500 is a hungry and miserable place for me. I don’t like it and don’t want to stay there any longer than necessary. Which is a great motivator to keep laying that Brick of the LBZ every single day. It reduces the length of the misery of the Consequence.
Now would be a good time to anticipate some pushback my views on Queen/Accountability that I frequently encounter by saying this: the Bricklaying system I just described is what works for me. If you have a different system, particularly one in which is not reliant up net-calories and the LBZ, I am not arguing with you. If your system works, use your system. My only contention is that for most men weight control requires a systematic approach because we have too much food that is too easy to get at too cheap a price to rely on exercise alone to stay Fit.
To Get Right, we have to serve the Queen.

Q-source - The Queen
No matter how hard and consistently a man may exercise, if his diet is haphazard his Fitness kingdom will not long stand. The Queen cannot be ignored, even by the strongest of Kings. Since we are talking about the Queen this week, I wanted to share some of my struggles with you today: sweet and tasty things. I know for certain that my fitness goals would be more easily attained if I paid attention and exercise some self-discipline into what I eat. So often I I find myself frustrated that I’m not making more progress in my fitness journey only to reflect on my failures of self-discipline. 

The reason is simple: more exercise means more calorie burn and more calorie burn means more hunger. The harder I exercise, the hungrier I get–the hungrier I get, the more I eat. That is the reason I can’t out-King my Queen. The faster I go on the Fitness road the higher my Guardrail needs to be to keep out of the ditch.

- Without a diet to complement, your exercise is worthless. Balancing it is even harder. Having the discipline to limit how much you eat, is what makes your King and Queen work well together. Hot take, there is no such thing as bad food, but there is a such thing as overeating foods that seem bad.

- Bricklaying. The act of creating good habits. Portion control and balance is key with bricklaying your Q to compliment your K. Pringles/chips/fries/popcorn, etc is addicting and can be hard to limit intake or easy to give in to the taste. Tracking calories and food groups is now easy by uploading your intake in an app that will calculate all of the stats depending on how much you eat. - Accountability. Keeping up with your Q and maintaining your intake is key for balance. If you don’t engage your K one day, your Q should reflect. It is easy to give in to temptation and go out to eat or not keep to your balance if traveling or through holidays, but keeping that shield lock during those speed bumps on your journey to Get Right is what will solidify those bricks you are laying. Q-source: The Queen (what you eat)
No matter how hard and consistently a man may exercise, if his diet is haphazard his Fitness kingdom will not long stand. The Queen cannot be ignored, even by the strongest of Kings.

In my own life, this has proven true, despite my best efforts and prideful thinking. Thoughts like “if I just run farther faster then I can eat what I want and still reach my fitness goals” have been prevalent in my life. For years, and years, I thought I could outwork my lack of discipline. My wife would help me where she could: she prepares amazing meals, is super conscientious of what our family consumes, and even tries to check me when I’m going for extra helpings of dessert. 

The phrase “you can’t out-king your queen” was one that was thrown around a lot when I was starting with F3, and I had NO IDEA what any of that meant. But it rings true. Trying to out exercise a crappy diet (or eating habits that lack discipline) is like swimming against the current - you’re not going to get any where.

COUNTERAMA

Today is March 1 - tomorrow, March 2, marks that 188th anniversary of Texas’s independence! 

On March 2, 1836, while Santa Anna’s Army of Operations continued to lay siege to the Alamo, the 60 delegates of the Consultation met at Washington-on-the-Brazos and ultimately signed their names to the Declaration of Independence, adding a link in the chain of events that would lead to a free and independent Texas before summer arrived. The document, similar in structure and language to the Declaration of Independence of the United States, declared, in part, as follows:

We, therefore, the delegates with plenary powers of the people of Texas, in solemn convention assembled, appealing to a candid world for the necessities of our condition, do hereby resolve and declare, that our political connection with the Mexican nation has forever ended, and that the people of Texas do now constitute a free, Sovereign, and independent republic, and are fully invested with all the rights and attributes which properly belong to independent nations; and, conscious of the rectitude of our intentions, we fearlessly and confidently commit the issue to the decision of the Supreme arbiter of the destinies of nations.

In honor of the brave signatories and in honor of Texas herself, instead of saying ‘halt’ at the end of our counts today, we will instead end with “AND one, two, three THE STARS ARE NIGHT, ARE BIG AND BRIGHT [CLAP CLAP CLAP CLAP] DEEP IN THE HEART OF TEXAS.”

Run & Gun

25 Cross-Court Bear Crawls (1 is 1) - Pax 1 runs faster than a spooked armadillo around the northwest loop of Jack and Dorothy Miller Park while Pax 2 performs Cross Court Bear Crawls (sideline to sideline). Pax 1 then tags Pax 2 out, and Pax 2 then runs the loop while Pax 1 picks up the Cross-Court Bear Crawls where Pax 2 left off. Continue until a combined 25 Cross-Court Bear Crawls are completed.

Q-source:
A man’s Right relationship with himself–his Fitness–begins with his body


Because it is his most fundamental piece of physical equipment, a man must get it and keep it in the normal upright position at all times if he wants to be Effective.

In fact, because Preparedness requires him to be ready for the unexpected (not just to get ready for the expected), the HIM (having turned Pro) is focused on gradually but consistently Accelerating his fitness level rather than merely staying in shape. Staying in shape is what Amateurs try to do.


Simultaneous Thangs 1, 2 and 3
Pax number off into 3 groups.


Double Apple Sauce Mosey
Run the small circle counterclockwise
leave group one at the Stone Henge for a 4 item Q-arama then do one lap and meet at the flags
send group two to the hill with sets of Bernie Sanders topped off with Q's choice x20 at top of hill (incline/decline merkins, burpees, sit-ups) until the other 2 groups are at the flags.
leave group three at the basketball  tennis court for a 3 item Q-arama with a suicide b/t each one


Q-source cont
A man maintains Fitness for reasons outside of himself
A man who has turned Pro doesn’t exercise to get good at exercising. His goal is Preparedness, a far broader and deeper objective than just feeling strong and looking good on the beach (although there is nothing wrong with either of those two things). The HIM stays in strict physical training to get a crown that will last forever. Thus, there is an eternal purpose in what he does. He is building a kingdom of Preparedness within which he intends other people to safely dwell. He knows that fatigue makes cowards of us all.


The goal of the King is to constantly increase 3S2T: Speed, Strength, Stamina, Toughness (physical) and Toughness (mental).
These are the aspects of a HIM’s physical kingdom that enable him to do the things he must do to be a Leader. It’s not really very complicated, how can a man be much of a Leader if he gets smoked pulling his family’s luggage off the baggage carousel and carrying it to the minivan? What will a son learn from a father who can’t play catch with him in the backyard for more than five minutes without having to sit down?

It doesn’t get easier gtting up early for BDs or choosing to get right. If this, choosing the red pill toward ms acceleration, was easy everyone would do it and the world would be a lot better place, but daily commitment to excellence is difficult yet allowing it to do its good work it will make our acceleration a sure thing. 

For a PAX to improve and break out of being a Mascot, he must have commitment. Commitment to his fitness, fellowship, and faith. 

Young men- pay attention to to the older PAX. It does not get easier to wake up early in the morning, but there is one this older men have that will motivate them and that is wisdom. Wisdom is seeing life from a perspective that transcends our current circumstances. It is time at work with both success and failure. ALAMO SIEGE INTRO
188 years ago today, on the morning of February 22, 1836, a garrison of about 180 Texas patriots, who were gathered in a caved in mission in San Antonio, woke up to the last peaceful morning of their lives. The next morning, the Centralist leader Santa Anna’s Army of Operations would besiege the Alamo and subject it to near constant cannon fire. However, the small group of brave volunteers, which included David Crockett, William Barret Travis, Jimmy Bowie, and Juan Seguin, would defend the fort in the face of certain defeat and imminent death. Today, we’re honoring their legacy with an Alamo-themed BD.


THANG 1 - Crockett’s Pallisade - 15 mins

Col. David Crockett and his Tennessee Vols were stationed by Col. Travis at the famous palisade, which was the weakest point in the Alamo walls, as it was made up of a picket of mesquite logs. However, the dead shot of Crockett and his volunteers made it unapproachable during the siege. So, let’s defend the Pallisade!

Each team chooses one member to play rock paper scissors. Winner chooses: 

Top of the hill 
Or 
Bottom of the hill

We then have 3 minutes to explain to each of our teams individually our objective, without suggesting a specific strategy, allowing our team to collaborate on a strategy. 

Team 1: Stands on top of the hill at eidelweiss. They each hold a cinderblock above their head as long as they can (5 minute limit).
If the cinderblock drops below the top of their head they have to set it down, and it becomes available for capture. Pax that lose their cinderblock lay on the ground like they are dead. Once the last cinderblock hits the ground the timer stops. 

Team 2: Waits at the bottom of the hill in plank position. 
Once a cinderblock block drops the whole team does 5 merkins (IC) and then one PAX runs up the hill and brings the cinderblock down the hill. Once the last cinderblock hits the grounds no more captures can be made and cinderblocks remain where they are. 

Then we switch sides and do the same thing. 

We determine the winner by the following equation: 

Time points - cinderblocks lost

1 minute = 100 points 
2 minutes = 200 points 
3 minutes = 300 points 
4 minutes = 400 points 
5 minutes = 600 points 

You have to reach the threshold of the next minute to get the next point level. 

Cinderblocks obtained -10 points 

So a team that reaches 3:30 and looses 4 cinderblocks would get 260 points. 

A team that reaches 3 minutes and drops all of their cinderblocks simultaneously (making them unavailable for capture) would get 300 points. 

A team that gets to 4 minutes but looses 8 cinderblocks gets 320 points. 

There are different ways to win but the Q’s don’t get to choose the strategy. They are responsible for articulating the mission and the team is responsible for devising the plan.

<band:refer user_key="AADWGp-pp3_FP4k_1gR2mt8k">SCUBA Steve</band:refer> offered some EXCELLENT improvements to this one, so if anyone ever wants to use this in a BD, I can tell you how to make it way better. Thanks Scuba!

THANG 2 - Loading the Cannon - 5 mins

Capt. Almoron Dickinson commanded the artillery at the Alamo, including the massive 18 pounder. During the final battle, Capt. Dickinson would famously attempt to turn the cannon to face the Alamo gates and blast the swarming enemy. In his honor, we’re going to load the old 18 ponder and fire it at the Sad Clown Army.

Both Teams begin at the bottom of the hill with one Cindy per pax. The objective is to cycle as many “rounds” of cindies through the “cannon” as possible in 5 mins. 

At “exercise” all PAX begin side straddle hops. Pax at the start of the line must murder bunny a Cindy to the top of the hill. Once at the top, he must lead his team in one of three exercises: 

a. Seven burpees on Q
b. 20 carolina dry docks in cadence
c. 10 merkins in cadence

If the Pax at the top misspeaks/fails to count properly, or if the pax fail to count while exercising, the Q pax restarts the exercise conpletely.

“Next exercise is … [PAX repeat]“
“Starting positions move.”
“In cadence/On Q … [PAX repeat]”
“And exercise.”

If on Q, call is “DOWN” with all Pax counting the rep.

If in cadence, Q cals “1, 2, 3,” and PAX count “ONE!” or “HALT.” Q should be sure to clearly inflect on final rep.

Once reps are completed, the cannon is considered loaded and fired. The pax resume side straddle hops. Q pax crawl bears down the hill while next pax murder bunny’s the next cannonball up the hill for BOHICA. Continue for 5 minutes. 

A pax cannot repeat an exercise until all three have been done at least once. If all cindies are at the top, all pax run up the hill, grab a cindy, and restart. Team with most rounds “loaded and fired” wins.

The goal here was to put all pax in a position to lead properly and clearly. And by God, they did. We had a couple of restarts, but those helped PAX learn to call cadence and exercises under standard BD pressure.

William Barret Travis.

Love is the accelerant of Preparedness
Each QPoint is a simple call to a difficult action that is designed to help the Q lay the Bricks necessary to form the Guardrails that will enable him to accelerate his G3L throughout his entire life. We call this process of Preparedness Bricklaying , and we know that it is not easy. It requires both the knowledge that change is required and the willingness to make it. While the former can be learned through Schooling (something every man is accustomed to doing), the latter requires a change of heart (something very few men do in the course of their lives).

Heart change requires passion, and by that we mean the willingness to suffer through the obstacles that always appear in the path of any Movement toward Advantage. Nothing good comes easily, nor should it, for it is what a man learns about himself during a difficult journey that makes him an Effective guide for those that come afterward. It is not the just the willingness to take the journey that makes a leader great, it is the quality of the map he draws along the way and his desire to share it with others for their Advantage.

nothing a man attains in his life has any value whatsoever until the very moment that he freely gives it away. That is the moment he transitions from being merely a leader into being a great leader.

The Q’s commitment to Preparedness will only take him so far down the road to greatness. He could have the heart of a lion and still fail for lack of a critical ingredient, and that is love. If he does not love the people he leads more than he loves himself he cannot put their interests above his own. And that is what Preparedness is ultimately about–the Q’s willing readiness to answer the unexpected call to subordinate his personal benefit for the benefit of those who depend upon him.
